setting: Bir tasinma (nakliyat) sirketiyle telefonda fiyat alma ve tarih ayirtma
context_line: You will hear a woman arranging a house move with a removals company.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Good afternoon, Hartfield Removals. How can I help you?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Hi there. I'm moving house next month, and I wanted to get a quote — and book a date, if I can.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Of course. I'll take a few details and then we can talk about prices. Could I have your name first?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: It's Petra Haugland.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Haugland. Would you mind spelling the surname for me?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Not at all. That's Haugland — H-A-U-G-L-A-N-D.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Thank you. And a phone number we can reach you on, on the day itself?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: The best one's my mobile — oh seven six three three, double four one, nine oh two.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Got that. And where are we moving you from?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Flat nine, Selby Court. Everyone round here says Selby Lane, but that's only the footpath at the side — the postal address is Weir Street.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Weir Street, then. Which floor are you on?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Second floor. And before you ask, there's no lift, I'm afraid.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: I'll make a note of it. Stairs change the time rather than the price. And where are you going to?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: A place called Ashcombe. It's about forty minutes north of here, just off the main road.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: We cover Ashcombe, that's no trouble at all. Is that another flat?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: No, a house this time — three bedrooms. That's rather the point. I did the last move myself with a hired van and two friends.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Very wise. And what date did you have in mind?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Saturday the third of October. It's been in my diary for weeks.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: I can do the third, but two warnings. Saturdays carry a surcharge, and that weekend is the start of half term round here, so the roads will be slow. If you can be flexible, the Friday — the second — is quieter and it's cheaper.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Actually, the Friday would work. I've got leave I have to use up anyway. Let's say the second.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Booked in. Now, before we quote properly, we'd normally send someone out to look at what you're taking. It only takes twenty minutes or so.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: When could that happen?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: We've a slot on Tuesday at half past ten. Sorry — ignore that, it's just gone. The next one free is Tuesday at eleven.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Eleven suits me better anyway.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Right. In the meantime, an estimate. For a three-bedroom move over that sort of distance, with two men and a large van, you're looking at three hundred and forty pounds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: And if I wanted you to do the packing as well?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: That takes it to four hundred and ten. It buys you boxes, tape, paper and two of our staff for the morning before.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Either way, the boxes themselves come free — we drop off twenty of them a week before the move, and you only pay for any extra ones you need.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Twenty should be plenty. There is one thing I'm nervous about, though. I've got a glass display cabinet that belonged to my grandmother.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: We build a wooden crate for anything of that sort. It's the one kind of item we won't simply wrap in blankets and hope.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: That's a relief. How long will the whole thing take?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: For a job that size I'd normally say about five hours. With your stairs at one end, call it six.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: And what time would you arrive?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: The crew will be with you between eight and half past. They'll ring when they leave the depot.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Is there a deposit?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: There is — fifty pounds to hold the date, and the balance on the day. I'll email you a payment link this afternoon. We don't take card details over the phone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Understood. Is there anything I need to sort out at my end?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Two things. The van's seven metres long, so if there's nowhere to stand it outside you'll need a parking permit from the council, and they want at least three working days' notice.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: There's a loading bay outside, but I'll ring them to be on the safe side.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Sensible. The other thing is what we can't carry: no paint, no aerosols and nothing out of the freezer. That's the insurance rather than us being difficult.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Speaking of which — are my things actually covered?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Everything's insured as standard up to a thousand pounds per item. If anything's worth more than that, mention it to the surveyor on Tuesday and we'll list it separately.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: The cabinet might well be. I'll ask him.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Please do. And one more thing you might find useful: if the new place isn't ready, we'll store your things free of charge for the first fortnight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: That is good to know. The keys are supposed to come through on the Thursday, but you never quite know, do you?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: You never do. Can I ask how you heard about us?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: My neighbour used you in the spring and hasn't stopped talking about it since.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: I'll pass that on. Right — your job number is four one seven eight, and the confirmation will be in your inbox within the hour.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Four one seven eight. Thanks very much for your help.
